observations: body L1-L20: every line of the quotation of al-Khāzinī opens with a guillemet; the quotation ends in L20. The guillemet before «staverit» (L4) prints deformed, like an x; a speck stands in the right margin beside L1.

body L10-L11: the Arabic phrase «وقسمناه على السبق المرئي لتلك الساعة خاصة دون سبقه الحقيقي», ‘and we divided it by the apparent precession of that hour alone, not by its true precession’, is divided between the lines, within the parentheses of the Latin. The lam of «السبق» (L11) prints broken, the top of its stem 1.6 pt apart like a dot, so that the word looks like «انسبق». The print sets L11 1.1 pt lower than the even spacing of L10 and L12.
body L16, L22, L28, L38-L39: the dashes measure 10.0, 10.1, 9.4, 9.7 and 9.6 pt.
body L20-L21: «al–murattabah» has a long dash (4.2 pt), and so has «133,r.–134,v.» (5.4 pt); «Ḥabash» is letter-spaced.
body L22, L38: the hyphens of «22-26» and «31-33» measure 3.7 and 3.5 pt.

body L24-L28: a heavy bracket opens the addition (L24) and another closes it (L28). The formulas are right: ½ (33′ 40″ + 35′ 20″) = ½ · 69′ = 34′ 30″ and ½ (31′ 20″ + 29′ 30″) = ½ · 60′ 50″ = 30′ 25″, with the diameters of p. 58 of the translation: the Sun 31′ 20″ in the apogee and 33′ 40″ in the perigee, the Moon 29′ 30″ (29′ ½) and 35′ 20″ (35′ ⅓). The translation, p. 106, notes 1-4, gives the codex 0° 36′ 39″ and 0° 34′ 36″ and Plato 0° 54′ 30″ (0° 54′ 53″ in note 3) and 0° 30′ 35″: Plato's upper limit in note 1 differs from 34′ 30″ only in the tens of the minutes, and his lower limit lies within 10″ of 30′ 25″. The equals signs of L26-L27 measure 9.4-10.0 pt; each piece of the two formulas is placed as printed.

body L29-L37: Nallino's addenda (Part I, p. LXXV) note that the passage belongs not to the Alfonsine Tables themselves but to the canons written for them by Santritter (cf. his preface, p. XXXVI, note 7). «Albategni» (L29) and «Alphonsi» (L35) are letter-spaced; «visa. et» (L32) is printed with a small et after the full stop.

body L39: the dots are five; the passage quoted is the translation, p. 106, l. 31-33, «Si hoc deprehendere calculo mavis ... ita calculus verior fit», and the heavy bracket opens an addition that continues on p. 282.
notes_left L1-L2: «Albatenii» (L1) is letter-spaced; «al–Khāzinī» (L2) has a long dash (4.3 pt). The rule between the two columns of the notes prints faint and broken.
notes_right L1-L3: «Al-Battānī» and «al-Battānī» have hyphens (3.1 and 3.0 pt), and so have «7-» and «-11» (3.4 and 3.2 pt). The signature 36 stands at the foot of the page, at the right.
